title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
abstract: arXiv:2611.14017v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-horizon personalized agents maintain an evolving memory by continuously deciding what to add, modify, or discard. However, learning an optimal update policy remains challenging. Conventional training relies solely on terminal question-answering accuracy, yielding a coarse feedback signal that treats all intermediate updates identically. Furthermore, update utility is inherently user-specific, as identical memory actions may yield opposite effects across different user personas. Existing methods fail to address this heterogeneity, relying on globally shared evaluation standards with at most a single scalar intermediate reward. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Personalized Memory Rubrics} (\textbf{PMR}), a framework that translates terminal feedback into fine-grained, per-step, and per-user credit assignment. translated_title: 个性化记忆量规：通过量规引导的信用分配学习每个用户应该记住什么
translated_abstract: 长时程个性化智能体通过持续决定添加、修改或丢弃哪些内容来维护一个不断演化的记忆。然而，学习最优的更新策略仍然充满挑战。传统训练仅依赖最终的问答准确率，由此产生的粗粒度反馈信号对所有中间更新一视同仁。此外，更新效用本质上是用户特定的，因为相同的记忆操作在不同用户画像下可能产生截然相反的效果。现有方法未能解决这种异质性，它们依赖全局共享的评估标准，且最多只有一个标量形式的中间奖励。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了个性化记忆量规（PMR），这是一个将终端反馈转化为细粒度的、按步骤且按用户的信用分配框架。PMR将评估分解为两个层次：一层是通用的，用于捕获跨用户画像的失败模式；另一层是每个用户自适应的……
tldr: 该论文提出个性化记忆量规（PMR）框架，将终端问答反馈转化为细粒度、按步骤且按用户自适应的信用分配，解决了长时程个性化智能体记忆更新策略训练中反馈信号粗粒度与用户间异质性两大难题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Personalized Memory Rubrics (PMR), a framework that translates terminal question-answering feedback into fine-grained, per-step, and per-user credit assignment to train memory update policies for long-horizon personalized agents, addressing coarse feedback signals and user-specific heterogeneity.
